grammar.title: Separable verbs – the prefix goes to the end
grammar.meaning: Many verbs have a prefix that separates from the verb in a main clause.
grammar.rule: In a main clause the conjugated verb stands in position 2 and the prefix goes to the end. In the Perfekt, -ge- stands between prefix and verb. With a modal verb the infinitive stays together at the end.

patterns.label: present
patterns.form: an|fangen → Die Besprechung fängt um neun an.

grammar.contrast: Inseparable prefixes (be-, ver-, er-, ent-) never separate: Ich verstehe die Aufgabe.
